classification.difficultyReason: Interpret 25% loss as 75% of the excess temperature remaining, calibrate the taught cooling model and solve a logarithmic equation for elapsed time.

content.prompt: A saucepan of water is brought nearly to the boil then removed from the heat. The temperature reaches $95^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and room temperature is a constant $25^\circ\mathrm{C}$. If the water has lost $25\%$ of its excess heat after $2.5$ minutes, find how long it will take for it to cool down to $30^\circ\mathrm{C}$. Give your answer in minutes to 2 decimal places.

answer.short: $22.93$ minutes after removal from the heat.
answer.worked:
Using $T=25+Ae^{-kt}$, where $t$ is measured in minutes and $k>0$:
$$\begin{align*}95&=25+A\\A&=70\end{align*}$$
The initial excess temperature is $95-25=70^\circ\mathrm{C}$. After $2.5$ minutes, $75\%$ of this excess remains:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Remaining excess temperature}&=0.75\times70\\&=52.5^\circ\mathrm{C}\\T(2.5)&=25+52.5\\&=77.5^\circ\mathrm{C}\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}77.5&=25+70e^{-2.5k}\\52.5&=70e^{-2.5k}\\e^{-2.5k}&=\frac34\\k&=\frac1{2.5}\ln\left(\frac43\right)\\&=\frac25\ln\left(\frac43\right)\end{align*}$$
Thus $T=25+70e^{-kt}$ with this exact value of $k$. For $T=30^\circ\mathrm{C}$:
$$\begin{align*}30&=25+70e^{-kt}\\5&=70e^{-kt}\\e^{-kt}&=\frac1{14}\\t&=\frac{\ln(1/14)}{-k}\\&=\frac{5\ln14}{2\ln(4/3)}\\&\approx22.93\text{ minutes}.\end{align*}$$
